title: The School That Puts the Kids in Charge

blanks.sentence: Students help decide who works at the school by _____.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Decisions and daily work

blanks.sentence: Running the school is intended to teach pupils _____.
Other pupils check prices; one student manages the _____.
Doing the accounting lets students see the school's _____, not just a practice exercise.
Compared with her previous school, one pupil can now develop _____ with friends.
Trying different activities may help pupils discover their personal _____.
Children give a positive _____ when adults place trust in them.
One observer describes the school as partly _____ despite its unusual approach.

multipleChoice.question: What best describes the students' role in the school's operation?
options: They advise teachers on rules while adults handle most daily decisions.
They take responsibility for decisions and tasks across school life.
They manage food purchases while staff make the school's rules.
They choose new staff but leave student discipline to teachers.

multipleChoice.question: Which arrangement would best fit the school's way of teaching responsibility?
options: Giving pupils extra talks about why everyday school duties matter.
Asking pupils to watch support staff organise their daily work.
Letting pupils choose a job to discuss in a classroom presentation.
Putting pupils in charge of arranging the school's cleaning rota.

multipleChoice.question: What does the description of food shopping show about student responsibility?
options: Pupils help buy food for the whole school, with an adult accompanying them.
Pupils compare menus for different classes before an adult buys the food.
Pupils purchase food independently for a small group of classmates.
Pupils check food prices after an adult has chosen what to purchase.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the pupil interested in accounting enjoy managing the food records?
options: The task gives her a break from studying school subjects.
The task allows her to supervise the other market shoppers.
The task lets her work with actual purchases and spending.
The task prepares her to teach accounting to younger pupils.

multipleChoice.question: How does the pupil contrast her former school with the Bamboo School?
options: Her former school offered practical tasks, while her current school stresses classroom lessons.
Her former school stressed individual work, while her current school avoids lessons.
Her former school offered leadership roles, while her current school limits them.
Her previous school centred on lessons; her current one also offers practical experience.

multipleChoice.question: What does the account of adults and children suggest about the school's approach?
options: It transfers classroom teaching to children while adults manage activities outside.
It keeps adult authority in all areas but invites student suggestions.
It combines familiar classroom teaching with unusual student control outside it.
It lets each class decide whether teachers or pupils should lead lessons.

multipleChoice.question: What further responsibility is mentioned alongside the pupils' schoolwork?
options: They also have a regular commitment to unpaid work for the community.
They must complete community work before joining ordinary lessons.
They spend most of each school week on community work.
They choose whether community work replaces classroom lessons.
